subject: Inline opt-out tagging + subprocessor zoning for no-derivative commitments
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@medsy.com>

Cc: legal@medsy.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Operationalising 'no-derivative' per-prompt opt-out + EU-only subprocessors

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal has pushed back on our standard DPA because we need the following operational guarantees before we can sign: 1) a per-interaction opt-out flag so that any prompt/response marked by our clients is excluded from model improvement (we call it a "no-derive"/"no-derivative" signal), 2) clear evidence that any subprocessor handling our data is EU-resident (or we get an onshore routing option), and 3) a straightforward audit package that shows requests flagged as no-derivative are never used in training pipelines.

Can you (or ops) sketch an implementation approach and a timeline? Legal also asked whether this can be enforced at the API layer with an HTTP header or must be handled later in the pipeline. We attached a rough DPA redline with comments.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we need a response to procurement by end of next week.

— Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Product, MedSy Health

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operationalising 'no-derivative' per-prompt opt-out + EU-only subprocessors

Hi Aisha — thanks for laying this out. We can support the requirements, and I wanted to propose a pragmatic, operational plan so procurement and legal have something concrete to review. High-level proposal (details attached in ops-design PDF):

- Inline opt-out tag: support an explicit request-level header and body flag (X-Redwood-No-Derivative: true / json field "no_derivative": true). This is enforced at the API gateway and flows through to the serving runtime and telemetry.
- Traffic-light enforcement: each request is assigned a traffic-light status (green = can be considered for improvement, amber = quarantined for ops review, red = no-derivative). Red requests are routed to an isolated processing lane where ephemeral KV is used and logs are tagged as non-training.
- Subprocessor zoning: we will provide a subprocessor map and an option to enable an "EU-only processing" tenant for your account which pins routing to EU-resident hosts and onshore subprocessors.
- Audit/evidence pack: automated evidence exports showing request IDs, header values, logs, and confirmation they were excluded from any model training jobs. We can produce certificates for a sample window or provide periodic attestations.

Timeline suggestion: prototype gating + header enforcement in 2 weeks; end-to-end ops + attestations in 4 weeks; formal runbook and DPA attachment in 6 weeks. We attached an ops-design PDF that shows the runtime flow and audit hooks.

I'll loop in David (security/legal touchpoint) and Kimberly (ops/product) to add detail and confirm the DPA language.

Next steps: 1) confirm your preferred enforcement mechanism (header vs body field), 2) confirm EU-only routing requirement scope (all accounts vs specific project), 3) pick a sample week for the evidence pack.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Product Manager — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Aisha — adding legal/controls perspective and suggested DPA language.

Key points for contracts:
- Definition: we suggest the term "No-Derivative Interaction" defined as any API request annotated with a mutually-agreed flag (X-Redwood-No-Derivative or JSON field).
- Contractual commitment: Redwood will not use No-Derivative Interactions for model improvement, model selection, or training, except to the extent necessary for debugging an active customer support issue (with prior notice and redaction).
- Evidence: Redwood will produce a quarterly attestation and a one-time evidence pack for initial onboarding. Evidence pack contents: request IDs, timestamps, header/body flags, subprocessor hostnames, and a signed statement by our operations lead.
- Subprocessors: we will add a "EU-only processing" addendum that pins compute and subprocessors to EU-resident vendors. Any change in subprocessor zoning will trigger 30-day notice and an update to the attestation.

We have redlined clause language in the attached DPA_redline_medsy_20260325.docx. A couple of practical notes: routing by header at the API gateway is the cleanest for enforcement (we can route to isolated pools and ensure that telemetry pipelines mark data as excluded). Please note that per-request flags require the customer to consistently set the flag — we can help with SDKs and server-side validation.

If MedSy wants the strongest technical guarantee, we recommend combining: 1) header enforcement + isolated processing lane, 2) onshore KMS key for encryption-at-rest for EU-only mode, and 3) periodic cryptographic proofs of deletion for any retained ephemeral artifacts.

If that sounds acceptable, we can hand this language to your legal team and prepare the attestation template.

— David Kim
Head of Security & Privacy Operations
Redwood Inference
